topics.title: Home
topics.body:
Welcome to **SquatClient**, a graphical MU* client with a TinyFugue-style scripting language and Lua. This help browser is built into the app: it works offline and everything in it is searchable.

## Where to start

- New here? Read [Getting started](help:getting-started).
- Want to connect to a game? See [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting).
- Want your sessions to survive closing the app? See [Squatter](help:squatter).
- Looking for a key? See [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys).
- Want to write triggers and macros? Start with [the scripting language](help:scripting), then [Lua scripting](help:lua).

## Using this help

| To do this             | Do this                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Open help              | type `/help`, press F1 (Cmd-? on macOS), choose Help in the menu, or click the **?** button                                 |
| Open a topic           | `/help def`, `/help keys`, `/help squatter` (a leading `/` is fine: `/help /def`)                                           |
| Search                 | type in the search box, or `/help some words`                                                                               |
| Move around            | click the topic tree, follow links, or press Alt-Left and Alt-Right for back and forward                                    |
| Jump to the search box | press `/`                                                                                                                   |
| Close                  | press Escape                                                                                                                |
| Try an example         | every code block has **Copy** and **Insert into input** buttons; Insert puts the text on your input line without sending it |

## Topics

- [Getting started](help:getting-started): first launch, quick connect, your first world.
- [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting): TLS, encodings, logins, passwords.
- [Squatter](help:squatter): persistent sessions with `squatterd`.
- [Using the client](help:using): output, scrollback, input editing, tabs, themes, colours.
- [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys)
- [Settings reference](help:settings)
- [Commands](help:commands): everything you can type that starts with `/`.
- [The scripting language](help:scripting): macros, triggers, expressions, hooks.
- [Lua scripting](help:lua): the `squat.*` API.
- [Compatibility notes](help:compat): how this relates to TinyFugue.
- [About and credits](help:about)

Please note that SquatClient's scripting language is an original implementation inspired by [TinyFugue](help:about#tinyfugue), written by Ken Keys.

topics.title: Getting started
topics.body:
## First launch

When SquatClient starts with no connection open you see an empty window with two buttons:

- **Worlds** opens the world manager, your saved connections.
- **Quick connect** connects to a host and port without saving anything.

The window has a tab bar on top (one tab per connection), the output pane in the middle, a single input line below it and a status bar at the bottom.

## Quick connect

1. Click **Quick connect** (or press Cmd-N / Ctrl-N).
2. Enter the **Host** and **Port**, for example `startrekkin.net` and `1701`.
3. Tick **Use TLS** only if the game offers an encrypted port.
4. Press **Connect**.

A new tab opens and the game's greeting appears. Type into the input line at the bottom and press Enter to send.

## Your first world

Saved worlds remember the host, port, TLS settings, encoding and an optional login. The default world is **startrekkin.net:1701**, a good place to try the client.

1. Open the world manager with Ctrl-O (or the tab-bar button).
2. Select a world, or add a new one.
3. Fill in the details (see [Connecting and worlds](help:connecting)).
4. Double-click a world to connect.

## Things to try next

- Scroll up with PageUp. Output pauses while you read and a **--More--** marker shows in the status bar. Press End or use the jump button to return to live output. See [Using the client](help:using#scrollback-and-pausing).
- Search the output with Cmd-F or Ctrl-Shift-F.
- Type `/help keys` to see the editing keys; they follow Emacs and TinyFugue.
- Try a first trigger. This highlights any line with "dragon" in it:

```
/def -t'*dragon*' -ahC#ff4040 dragon
```

More in [the scripting language](help:scripting).

## Keeping sessions alive

By default a world connects **Direct** and ends when you quit. To keep connections running while the app is closed, set up a squatter and choose it in a world's **Connect via** setting; see [Squatters and routing](help:squatter/routing).

topics.title: Squatters and routing
topics.body:
## The model

- A **squatter** is a saved _remote relay_: a `squatterd` you run on a server. You can save **many** squatters, for example `home-vps` and `work-box`.
- Each **world** chooses how it connects with its **Connect via** setting:
  - **Direct**: straight from this computer to the game. The connection ends when the app closes.
  - **A saved squatter**: the squatter holds the game connection. It survives closing the app, and when you reattach everything you missed is replayed.
- Different worlds can therefore use different squatters, and some can be direct, all at the same time.
- There is **one hop** for now: client, squatter, game. Chaining squatters, or a squatter going out through a proxy, is planned for later and is not available yet.

## Example

| World      | Connect via | What happens                                 |
| ---------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Star Trek  | home-vps    | held by `home-vps`; still connected tomorrow |
| Work MUSH  | work-box    | held by `work-box`                           |
| Quick test | Direct      | ends when you quit                           |

## Adding a squatter

1. On the server run `./squatterd --port 10327`.
2. On the server run `./squatterd pair` and note the one-time code and the fingerprint.
3. In SquatClient open the squatters dialog, choose **Add a squatter**, and enter the name, host, port and code.
4. Confirm that the TLS fingerprint shown matches the one `squatterd pair` printed, then **Trust and pair**.
5. In each world that should use it, set **Connect via** to the new squatter.

### When the port is firewalled

Reach the server over Tailscale (use its Tailscale address as the host), or through an ssh tunnel:

```
ssh -N -L 10327:127.0.0.1:10327 user@server
```

then add the squatter as `127.0.0.1` port `10327`. On the server start squatterd with `--bind 127.0.0.1 --insecure-loopback` as described in the squatterd README.

## Detaching and ended sessions

`/suspend` and `/detach` detach the squatter-held sessions; they keep running. An ended session is just history: nothing reconnects automatically, and the squatter stores no game passwords. See [Squatter](help:squatter#suspend-and-detach).

topics.title: Connecting and worlds
topics.body:
A **world** is a saved connection. Open the world manager with Ctrl-O, the menu (Session, Worlds) or the tab-bar button. Worlds are stored in a file in the SquatClient configuration folder; passwords never are.

## World fields

| Field                         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name                          | what the tab shows                                                                                                                                                    |
| Group                         | optional folder name used to group the list                                                                                                                           |
| Host and Port                 | where the game listens                                                                                                                                                |
| Connect via                   | **Direct** (from this computer, ends when the app closes) or any saved squatter that holds the connection for you; see [Squatters and routing](help:squatter/routing) |
| Encoding                      | how bytes from the game are decoded: UTF-8 (default) or Latin-1                                                                                                       |
| Use TLS                       | encrypt the connection                                                                                                                                                |
| Skip certificate verification | accept any certificate; only for games with self-signed certificates                                                                                                  |
| Connect automatically         | connect when the app starts                                                                                                                                           |
| Login template                | text sent after connecting; `{name}` and `{password}` are substituted                                                                                                 |
| Character name                | replaces `{name}`                                                                                                                                                     |
| Password                      | replaces `{password}`; stored in the OS keychain                                                                                                                      |
| Notes                         | free text                                                                                                                                                             |

## TLS

Tick **Use TLS** when the game offers a TLS port. Certificates are verified strictly by default. Some games use a self-signed certificate; for those, tick **Skip certificate verification**, understanding that it removes protection against someone impersonating the game.

## Encodings

UTF-8 is the default and handles accented letters, emoji and box-drawing characters. Some older games send Latin-1; if you see garbled accents, switch that world to Latin-1. You can set the default for new connections in [Settings](help:settings).

## Login templates

If a world has a login template the client sends it for you after connecting. A typical MUSH template is:

```
connect {name} {password}
```

## Passwords and the keychain

Game passwords are saved in the operating system keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, or the Secret Service on Linux), never in the worlds file; the file only records that a password exists. If the keychain cannot be reached, connecting to a world that needs a password fails with an error rather than sending an empty password. A squatter never stores your game passwords either: your client sends the login.

## Several connections

Each connection is a tab. Press Alt-1 to Alt-9 to switch, or Ctrl-Tab and Ctrl-Shift-Tab to cycle. A badge on a tab shows unread lines in background connections, and the status bar shows how many are active. Closing a tab disconnects it; an ended tab stays until you dismiss it, with the reason and the last text received.

## Scripting your worlds

The scripting language can also define and connect worlds; see `/addworld`, `/connect`, `/world` and `/fg` in [Commands](help:commands).

topics.title: Squatter
topics.body:
## What is squatterd?

**squatterd** is a small optional program that holds your game connections for you, in the spirit of `screen` or TinyFugue on a shell account. You run it on a machine that stays on. When you close SquatClient the game connection stays up, squatterd keeps recording what the game says, and the next time you attach it replays everything you missed and carries on live.

You do not need a squatter to use SquatClient. Without one, connections are **direct** and end when you quit the app.

What squatterd does **not** do:

- It **never logs in for you** and **stores no game passwords**. Your client sends the login lines.
- It **never reconnects automatically**. If the game connection ends, the session is shown as ended with the reason, and it stays ended until you dismiss it.

## Running it

On the machine that will hold your sessions (the engine repository builds the binary with `make build`):

```
./squatterd --port 10327
```

The default port is 10327, the connection is TLS, and data lives in `~/.squatterd`. To see the other options use `./squatterd --help`; for example `--bind` limits the address it listens on and `--data-dir` moves its files.

## Pairing

Pairing lets this copy of SquatClient talk to your squatter. It happens once per device.

1. On the squatter machine run:

   ```
   ./squatterd pair
   ```

   It prints a one-time **pairing code** such as `ABCD-EFGH` (valid for ten minutes), the TLS **fingerprint**, and a host and port hint.

2. In SquatClient open the squatters dialog (the tab-bar button), choose **Add a squatter**, and enter a name, the host, the port (10327 unless you changed it) and the pairing code. Press **Pair**.
3. Compare the fingerprint SquatClient shows with the one `squatterd pair` printed. If they match, press **Trust and pair**. If they differ, press **Reject**: something is between you and your server.

## Trusting the fingerprint

The squatter makes its own TLS certificate, so there is no certificate authority to vouch for it. SquatClient therefore uses _trust on first use_: you confirm the fingerprint once, and from then on that exact fingerprint is pinned. If it ever changes, the connection is refused. Only pair devices you trust: anyone who can pair can open connections to any host from the squatter machine, and `./squatterd revoke <deviceId>` removes a device.

## Using a squatter

In the world manager set **Connect via** to your squatter. Sessions you open that way live on the squatter. You can save several squatters and route different worlds through different ones; see [Squatters and routing](help:squatter/routing).

### /suspend and /detach

Type `/suspend` (or `/detach`) to let go of squatter-held sessions while leaving them running: the client goes idle, the sessions keep recording, and you resume later by attaching again, when everything you missed is replayed. Direct sessions cannot outlive the app, so for them `/suspend` can only hide the window and the connections stay live. If both kinds are open only the squatter-held sessions are detached.

Note: this behaviour is specified in the project design; if your build prints `/suspend (not available)`, simply close the app, and the squatter-held sessions carry on regardless.

### Ended sessions

When a game closes the connection, resets it or cannot be reached, the session becomes **ended**. The tab shows the reason, the time and the last text received, and the full history is kept. Choose **Connect again** to open a fresh connection or **Dismiss** to remove it. Nothing reconnects by itself.

## Security summary

- Transport: TLS with a pinned self-signed certificate.
- Authentication: your client holds an ed25519 key; the squatter remembers its public key.
- Pairing codes are single use and expire; repeated wrong codes lock out the sender for five minutes.
- If you reach the squatter through an ssh tunnel, point the client at the loopback address as described in the squatterd README.

topics.title: Using the client
topics.body:
## The window

- **Tab bar**: one tab per connection, plus buttons for worlds, quick connect, squatters, search, settings and help.
- **Output pane**: what the game says, plus your own typed lines and system messages.
- **Input line**: where you type. Lines starting with `/` are commands, anything else is sent to the game.
- **Status bar**: connection state, activity in other tabs, the pause marker, any fields your scripts add, and the clock.

## Output pane

Text keeps the colours and styles the game sends: bold, dim, italic, underline, strikethrough, blink and reverse. Colours can be the 16 theme colours, the 256-colour xterm palette, or 24-bit truecolour, and all of UTF-8 is displayed. Links the game marks up, and bare `http://` and `https://` addresses (if enabled in [Settings](help:settings)), are clickable and open in your system browser. Only web addresses are ever opened.

Select text with the mouse and copy it as usual.

## Scrollback and pausing

Recent output is kept in memory, up to the **scrollback lines** setting; older history is fetched on demand when you scroll up. Use PageUp and PageDown to scroll, or the mouse wheel.

When you scroll up, live output **pauses** so the text you are reading does not move (if _Pause output when scrolled up_ is on). The status bar shows **--More--** with a count of lines that arrived meanwhile. Press End (when the output has focus) or the jump button to return to live output. This replaces TinyFugue's `--More--` prompt.

## Searching

Press Cmd-F or Ctrl-Shift-F (Ctrl-F when the output has focus) to open the search bar. It offers previous and next match, case sensitivity and regular expressions, and searches the whole scrollback of the current tab.

## Editing the input line

The input line understands the Emacs editing keys TinyFugue users know. The full list is in [Keyboard shortcuts](help:keys). Highlights:

- Home/End or Ctrl-A/Ctrl-E move to the start or end.
- Ctrl-W and Alt-D delete words; Ctrl-K and Ctrl-U delete to the end or the whole line; Ctrl-Y pastes the last deletion.
- Shift-Enter inserts a new line so you can write several lines before sending.
- Pasting several lines sends them one by one.
- Escape clears the line.

### History

Up and Down (or Ctrl-P and Ctrl-N) walk through lines you sent earlier. If you typed something first, only lines starting with it are offered, so typing `/def` and pressing Up finds your last `/def` command.

### Passwords

Lines like `connect name password`, `create name password` and `@password ...` are recognised automatically and are never echoed, stored or logged by a squatter; the screen shows them masked (`connect name ********`). Use `/secret text` for anything else you must keep out of logs.

When the game turns off echo (for a password prompt) the input becomes a masked password field with a lock icon, history is disabled and what you type is not recorded.

## Tabs

Each connection has a tab. Use Alt-1 to Alt-9 or Ctrl-Tab to switch. Unread lines in background tabs show as a badge, and with desktop notifications on you also get notified. The small **x** on a tab disconnects it, or dismisses it if it has already ended.

## Themes

Pick a theme in [Settings](help:settings): **Dark**, **Light** or **High contrast**. A theme sets the text and background colours, the 16 ANSI colours and the colours of the window chrome. You can import your own theme as JSON. If some colour combinations are hard to read, set **Minimum contrast** (4.5 is the WCAG AA level) and the client nudges colours to meet it. The client respects your system's _reduce motion_ preference.

## Colours

By default SquatClient shows UTF-8 text with xterm-256 and 24-bit truecolour. Type `/colortest` to print every colour mode (16 colours, the full 256 grid, truecolor gradients, text styles and UTF-8) and compare it with another program.

**Why basic colours can differ between programs:** colours 0-15 (the plain `red`, `yellow`, ... and their bright versions) are not fixed: every terminal and theme chooses its own shades, and games that use them look different in different clients. Colours 16-255 (xterm-256) and truecolour are exact everywhere. SquatClient's default dark theme uses a classic terminal palette so a game that sends basic colours looks like it does in tinyfugue; if a slot looks wrong, change it in a custom theme (see below). _Bold text uses bright colours_ makes bold text switch to the bright variant of the 8 basic colours, as in many terminals. In scripts you can use all of these colours; see [Attributes](help:scripting/attributes).

## Accessibility

Dialogs trap keyboard focus and close with Escape, controls have labels, and _Screen-reader mode_ announces new lines to assistive technology. A "Skip to input" link is the first thing a keyboard user reaches.

topics.title: Keyboard shortcuts
topics.body:
On macOS, **Alt** means the Option key and **Cmd** the Command key. On other systems use Ctrl where Cmd is shown.

## Editing the input line

These are the default bindings of the input line. They follow Emacs and TinyFugue.

| Key                          | Action                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter                        | send the line                                           |
| Shift-Enter                  | insert a new line                                       |
| Tab                          | insert a tab character                                  |
| Escape                       | clear the input line                                    |
| Ctrl-A, Home                 | start of line                                           |
| Ctrl-E, End                  | end of line                                             |
| Ctrl-B, Left                 | back one character                                      |
| Ctrl-F, Right                | forward one character                                   |
| Alt-B, Ctrl-Left, Alt-Left   | back one word                                           |
| Alt-F, Ctrl-Right, Alt-Right | forward one word                                        |
| Backspace, Ctrl-H            | delete the character before the cursor                  |
| Delete, Ctrl-D               | delete the character under the cursor                   |
| Ctrl-W, Alt-Backspace        | delete the word before the cursor                       |
| Alt-D                        | delete the word after the cursor                        |
| Ctrl-K                       | delete to the end of the line                           |
| Ctrl-U                       | delete the whole line                                   |
| Ctrl-Y                       | paste the last deleted text                             |
| Ctrl-T                       | swap the two characters around the cursor               |
| Up, Ctrl-P                   | previous history line (prefix search on what you typed) |
| Down, Ctrl-N                 | next history line                                       |

Up, Down, Ctrl-P, Ctrl-N and Shift-Enter are disabled while a password is being typed.

## Windows and sessions

| Key                      | Action                                        |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| Alt-1 to Alt-9           | switch to session 1 to 9                      |
| Ctrl-Tab, Ctrl-Shift-Tab | next and previous session                     |
| Cmd-N, Ctrl-N            | quick connect (menu: Session, New Connection) |
| Ctrl-O, Cmd-O            | world manager                                 |
| Ctrl-, and Cmd-,         | settings                                      |
| Cmd-W                    | close the session                             |

## Output and search

| Key                  | Action                                                   |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| PageUp, PageDown     | scroll the output (pauses live output)                   |
| End (output focused) | jump to live output                                      |
| Cmd-F, Ctrl-Shift-F  | search the scrollback (Ctrl-F when the output has focus) |

## Help

| Key                 | Action                                |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| F1, Cmd-?           | open help                             |
| `/`                 | focus the help search box             |
| Up, Down            | move in the topic tree                |
| Right, Left         | expand, collapse in the tree          |
| Enter               | open the selected topic               |
| Alt-Left, Alt-Right | back, forward in help history         |
| Escape              | clear the search box, then close help |

You can change bindings from scripts with `/bind`; see [Macros: /def](help:scripting/macros-def).

topics.title: Settings reference
topics.body:
Open settings with Ctrl-, (Cmd-, on macOS), the menu (Session, Settings) or the gear button. Changes apply immediately.

| Setting                       | Meaning                                                                       | Default                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Theme                         | Dark, Light, High contrast, or an imported theme                              | Dark                                                |
| Import theme (JSON)           | add your own theme from JSON text                                             | none                                                |
| Font family                   | font stack for the output and input                                           | JetBrains Mono, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace |
| Font size (px)                | size of text in the output                                                    | 14                                                  |
| Scrollback lines in memory    | how many lines per tab are kept in memory; older history is fetched on demand | 20000                                               |
| Minimum contrast              | 0 turns it off; 4.5 meets WCAG AA; colours are adjusted to reach it           | 0                                                   |
| Default encoding              | UTF-8 or Latin-1 for new connections; a world can override it                 | UTF-8                                               |
| Show timestamps               | prefix each line with its time                                                | off                                                 |
| Bold text uses bright colours | bold basic colours become bright colours                                      | off                                                 |
| Make bare URLs clickable      | turn `http://` and `https://` text into links                                 | on                                                  |
| Pause output when scrolled up | freeze live output while you read older text                                  | on                                                  |
| Desktop notifications         | notify about activity in background tabs                                      | on                                                  |
| Screen-reader mode            | announce new lines to assistive technology                                    | off                                                 |

The scrollback size is applied when the app starts. Truecolour is always on.

Other places that hold settings: worlds ([Connecting and worlds](help:connecting)), squatters ([Squatter](help:squatter)) and scripts ([the scripting language](help:scripting)).

topics.title: Commands
topics.body:
Anything you type that starts with `/` is a command. Everything else is sent to the game.

## Handled by the app

| Command | Meaning                                                                |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/help` | open this help; `/help topic` opens a topic and `/help words` searches |

`/help` is handled by the window itself, before anything is sent to the engine, so it works even when no world is connected. The browser accepts TinyFugue-style names: `/help def`, `/help /def`, `/help expressions`, `/help triggers`.

## Handled by the engine

| Command               | Meaning                                                              |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/lua code`           | run a line of Lua; see [Lua scripting](help:lua)                     |
| `/load file`          | load a `.tf` script, or a `.lua` plugin when the name ends in `.lua` |
| `/reload`             | reload Lua plugins and the startup file                              |
| `/suspend`, `/detach` | detach squatter-held sessions; see [Squatter](help:squatter)         |
| `/secret text`        | send text without recording it anywhere (never echoed, stored or logged by a squatter); see [Passwords](help:using#passwords) |
| `/colortest`          | print every colour mode (16 colours, the full xterm-256 grid, truecolor gradients, text styles, UTF-8) to compare with a terminal; see [Colours](help:using#colours) |

## TinyFugue-style commands

The scripting language provides the rest. Open any of them with `/help name`.

| Area                | Commands                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Output              | `/echo` `/send` `/beep` `/notify` `/gag` `/hilite`                                                                          |
| Variables           | `/set` `/setenv` `/export` `/unset` `/let` `/listvar` `/shift`                                                              |
| Evaluation          | `/eval` `/test` `/return` `/break` `/builtin`                                                                               |
| Control flow        | `/if` `/elseif` `/else` `/endif` `/while` `/do` `/done` `/for`                                                              |
| Macros and triggers | `/def` `/undef` `/undefn` `/list` `/purge` `/enable` `/disable` `/trigger` `/trigpc` `/hook`                                |
| Keys                | `/bind` `/unbind` `/dokey`                                                                                                  |
| Files               | `/load` `/save` `/require` `/quote`                                                                                         |
| Timers              | `/repeat` `/ps` `/kill`                                                                                                     |
| Worlds              | `/addworld` `/connect` `/dc` `/fg` `/world` `/unworld` `/listworlds` `/listsockets` `/saveworld`                            |
| View                | `/limit` `/unlimit` `/relimit` `/recall` `/log` `/input` `/localecho` `/status_add` `/status_edit` `/status_rm` `/histsize` |
| Information         | `/version` `/features` `/restrict` `/exit` `/quit`                                                                          |

Start at [the scripting language](help:scripting), especially [Commands](help:scripting/commands), and see [Compatibility notes](help:compat) for which commands behave differently from TinyFugue.

topics.title: The scripting language
topics.body:
> **SquatClient's scripting language is an original implementation, inspired by and designed to be closely compatible with TinyFugue ("tf").** TinyFugue was written by **Ken Keys** (<https://tinyfugue.sourceforge.net>). Thank you, Ken, and thank you to the TinyFugue community for decades of documentation, scripts and answers. See [About and credits](help:about#tinyfugue).

SquatClient contains no TinyFugue source code and bundles none of its help text; it follows TinyFugue's documented behaviour and improves on it in a few places. If you know TinyFugue you will feel at home; the differences are listed in [Compatibility notes](help:compat).

## The language in one page

Lines that start with `/` are commands; everything else is text for the game. A script is a plain `.tf` file of commands that you `/load`.

```
/set greeting=Hello
/echo %greeting, world
/def -t'* tells you: *' -ahCgreen tell = /echo Got a tell from %P1
```

- A **macro** is a named command list made with `/def`. With `-t` it becomes a **trigger** that fires on matching game text; with `-h` it is a **hook** that fires on an event.
- **Variables** are set with `/set` and read with `%name` or `%{name}`.
- **Expressions** go in `$[...]` and `/if (...)`.

## Reference topics

The rest of this section is the reference for the language, one page per chapter. Use `/help name` to jump straight to a command or function, for example `/help def`, `/help strlen` or `/help expressions`.

Use the **Insert into input** button on any example to try it.

## Related

- [Lua scripting](help:lua), for structured plugins.
- [Compatibility notes](help:compat).
- [Commands](help:commands), the list of everything starting with `/`.

topics.title: Lua scripting
topics.body:
SquatClient embeds Lua 5.1 as a sandboxed second scripting language alongside [the TinyFugue-style language](help:scripting). Use Lua for larger, structured plugins and TF for quick triggers and for scripts you already have; the two can call each other.

Everything lives in the global table `squat`. Plugins are `.lua` files in the `plugins` folder of the SquatClient scripts directory and are loaded at start. Type `/reload` to reload them. You can also try code directly:

```
/lua squat.echo("hello from Lua")
```

The following pages are the full reference of the `squat.*` API.

topics.title: Compatibility notes
topics.body:
A short version of what matches TinyFugue, what is intentionally different, and what is out of scope. The full, authoritative matrix follows in the pages below this one.

## What matches

- The command syntax and most commands: `/def`, `/set`, `/let`, `/if`, `/while`, `/for`, `/eval`, `/test`, `/repeat`, `/quote`, `/load`, `/require` and more.
- Macro options `-t -m -h -p -n -F -g -a -P -b -w -E -c`, and glob, simple and regexp patterns.
- Substitution: `%{name}`, `%1`..`%9`, `%*`, `%L`, `%R`, `%P0..%P9`, `$[expr]`, `$(command)`.
- The expression language, its operators and most functions, and the hook names.
- The Emacs-style editing keys and history.

## What is intentionally different

- Inside expressions, `%x` and `%1` are **variable references**, never re-parsed as text. That prevents text from the game from injecting commands.
- `=~` and `!~` compare strings exactly; `=/` and `!/` are glob matches. There is no `%` operator: use `mod()`.
- Triggers fire **deterministically**: by priority, then definition order, and only one macro per priority unless `-F` is given. TinyFugue picks randomly among equals.
- Every glob wildcard of a trigger is available as `%P1`, `%P2`...
- A script file that contains a line that is not a command is an **error**; scripts never send text by accident.
- Backquote command substitution is not provided, because it implied a shell.
- Colour attributes also accept 256-colour indices, the `rgb` cube, `grayN` and `#rrggbb` truecolour.
- Every script run has a step budget, a time limit and nesting limits so a runaway macro cannot freeze the client.
- Regular expressions use Go (RE2) syntax.

## What is out of scope

SquatClient is a graphical client. Features that exist in TinyFugue only because it ran in a terminal are **not implemented and not planned**: line wrapping variables (`wrap`, `wrapsize`...), the terminal `--More--` prompt (replaced by pause-when-scrolled-up), screen modes (`/visual`, `/redraw`), terminal signals, terminal geometry, and the keyboard-buffer functions. Scripts that use them still load: the commands and variables are accepted and ignored. Shell commands (`/sh`) are not available.

## Status

The compatibility matrix was written from the public TinyFugue manual and has not yet been verified against a reference `tf` binary, so read "Done" as "implemented to the documented intent". Some features are planned: `/edit`, `/recordline`, `/watchdog`, the stream functions (`tfopen` and friends) and `%{-N}` ranges.

topics.title: Reference overview
topics.body:
`pkg/tf` implements a TinyFugue-style MU* client language. It is an original
implementation inspired by TinyFugue's documented behaviour; it is not
bug-for-bug compatible. Differences are listed in `TF-COMPAT.md`.

Scripts are plain text files (`.tf`). Everything below can be typed on the
input line, put in a script and `/load`ed, or run by triggers and hooks.

topics.title: Input lines, statements and scripts
topics.body:
- A line that starts with `/` is a **command**. Any other line is **text** and is
  sent to the world (not expanded, unless `/set sub=on`).
- A command line is split into **statements** at `;` and at `%;`. Separators
  inside `$[...]`, `$(...)` and `%{...}` do not split. `/def`, `/repeat` and
  `/eval` keep `%;` unsplit so that it separates statements when their body
  runs later:

  ```
  /def greet = /echo hello %; /echo again     ; the whole body is stored
  ```

  A plain `;` ends the `/def` itself. Text lines are never split at `;`.

- **Script files**: blank lines and lines starting with `;` are ignored; a line
  ending in `\` continues on the next line (leading blanks of the next line are
  dropped). Every other line must be a command (non-command lines in a file are
  an error: a script never sends text by accident). Blocks (`/if`, `/while`,
  `/do`, `/for`) may span lines and are collected until their `/endif` /
  `/done`.
- Errors print as `% message` through the host and the script keeps going,
  except that an error inside a loop body ends the loop. At most 20 errors are
  shown per run.

topics.title: Substitution
topics.body:
Performed on the arguments of ordinary commands and on every statement of a
macro body when it runs.

| Syntax                 | Meaning                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `%%`                   | a literal `%`                                                                                        |
| `%;`                   | a literal `;` (when it survives splitting)                                                           |
| `%name`, `%{name}`     | variable (local first, then global); unset is empty                                                  |
| `%1`..`%9`, `%{N}`     | positional parameters (words of the arguments)                                                       |
| `%*`                   | all arguments as typed; `%#` their count; `%0` the macro name                                        |
| `%PL` `%PR`            | text left / right of the last regexp match; `%L` is the last positional parameter, `%R` a random one |
| `%-N` `%{-N}` `%-L`    | all parameters but the first N / but the last                                                        |
| `%{sel-default}`       | the default when the selector expands to nothing                                                     |
| `%P0`..`%P9`, `%{P12}` | match parts: `P0` the whole match, `P1`.. captures                                                   |
| `%{?name}`             | `1` if the variable is set, else `0`                                                                 |
| `$[expr]`              | value of an expression                                                                               |
| `$(command)`           | what the command echoed (lines joined by spaces); if it echoed nothing, its `/return` value          |
| `$$`                   | a literal `$`                                                                                        |

Substitution is a single pass: substituted text is not rescanned, so text from
the MUD can never inject commands through `%*`. `/eval` expands its arguments
and then runs the result, which expands again:

```
/set cmd=/echo hi
/eval %cmd              ; runs /echo hi
/eval /echo %%{x}       ; first pass leaves %{x}, second pass expands it
```

**Triggers** receive `%*` = the line, `%1..` = its words, `%P0` = the whole match,
`%P1..` = glob wildcards or regexp groups in order, `%PL`/`%PR` for regexp
triggers.

topics.title: Expressions
topics.body:
Used by `$[...]`, `/test`, `/if`, `/elseif`, `/while`, `/do..while`, `/for`,
`/return`, `/def -E` and `test()`/`eval()`.

Values are integers (int64), floats, or strings. Text that looks like a number
is a number; arithmetic treats non-numeric text as 0. Truth: a non-zero number,
or a non-empty non-numeric string.

Operators, lowest to highest precedence:

|                              |                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `,`                          | sequence (value of the last)                                                             |
| `=` `:=` `+=` `-=` `*=` `/=` | assignment to a variable (right associative)                                             |
| `a ? b : c`                  | conditional                                                                              |
| `\|` `\|\|`                  | logical or (short-circuit, result 0/1)                                                   |
| `&` `&&`                     | logical and (short-circuit)                                                              |
| `==` `!=`                    | equal: numeric when both sides are numbers, else string compare                          |
| `=~` `!~`                    | exact string equal / not equal (never numeric)                                           |
| `=/` `!/`                    | glob match / no match: `str =/ "pat*"`                                                   |
| `<` `>` `<=` `>=`            | numeric when both numbers, else string order                                             |
| `+` `-`                      | add, subtract                                                                            |
| `*` `/`                      | multiply, divide (integer division when both are integers; division by zero is an error) |
| `!` `-` `+` `++x` `--x`      | unary, prefix increment                                                                  |
| `x++` `x--`                  | postfix                                                                                  |

Barewords are variables (`x`); `name(args)` calls a function; `{x}`, `{1}`, `{*}`,
`{#}` and `%x`, `%1`, `%*`, `%#`, `%{name}` read variables and parameters
**without** re-parsing the value as expression text (prefer these for script
input). There is no `%` operator (use `mod()`); `%` is not interpolated inside
string literals (use `strcat`). String literals use `"` or `'` with `\n \t \r \e
\\ \"` escapes. Numbers: `12`, `1.5`, `.5`, `1e3`, `0x1f`.

A user macro can be called like a function: `/def add = /return {1} + {2}` then
`$[add(2, 3)]`.

topics.title: Variables
topics.body:
- `/set name=value` (or `/set name value`) sets a **global**; if a **local** of
  that name exists in the running macro, the local is changed instead.
- `/let name=value` creates/sets a **local** that lives until the macro returns.
- `/setenv name=value` is `/set` plus marking it exported; `/export name` marks an
  existing one. `/unset name`. `/listvar [glob]`. `/set` alone lists everything.
- Names are `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. Values are strings that act as numbers
  when numeric.
- Behavioural variables read by the interpreter: `gag` and `hilite` (set to `0`
  to disable gag/hilite effects), `matching` (default `/def` match mode),
  `hiliteattr` (attribute used by `/hilite`, default `h`), `sub` (`on` expands
  `%` in typed text), `quiet`, `TZ` (`UTC` or a fixed offset such as `UTC+2`,
  `-0530`, used by `ftime`/`mktime`), `histsize`. Others from TinyFugue are
  accepted as ordinary variables (see `TF-COMPAT.md`).
- The host can export and import all globals as JSON (`ExportVars`,
  `ImportVars`).

topics.title: Macros: /def
topics.body:
```
/def [options] [name] [= body]
```

The body is stored unexpanded and expanded each time the macro runs. Calling
`/name args` runs it with `%1..` set from `args`. A macro may also be a
trigger, a hook, or a key binding. Options (no space between the letter and its
value; quote values containing spaces with `'..'`, `".."` or `{..}`):

| Option                     | Meaning                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-t<pattern>`              | trigger on received text matching the pattern                     |
| `-m<glob\|simple\|regexp>` | pattern style (default `glob`, or `$matching`)                    |
| `-h<HOOK [argpattern]>`    | run when the hook fires (optional glob over the hook's arguments) |
| `-p<n>`                    | priority (default 0; higher runs first)                           |
| `-n<shots>` / `-1`         | delete the macro after that many firings                          |
| `-F`                       | fall-through: after firing, let lower-priority matches fire too   |
| `-g`                       | gag (hide) matching lines                                         |
| `-a<attrs>`                | highlight the whole line (see section 6); `g` in the attrs gags   |
| `-P<n><attrs>`             | highlight part `n` (0 whole match, 1..9 capture/wildcard)         |
| `-b<key>` / `-k<key>`      | bind to a key name (the engine delivers key names)                |
| `-w<world>`                | only active for that world                                        |
| `-E<expr>`                 | extra condition; must be true for the macro to fire               |
| `-c<percent>`              | fire with that probability (0 or 100 = always)                    |
| `-i`                       | invisible: `/purge` without arguments skips it                    |

Patterns:

- **glob** matches the _whole_ line: `*` any text, `?` one character,
  `[a-z]` / `[^a-z]` classes, `{red|blue}` alternatives, `\*` a literal. Write
  `*dragon*` to match anywhere. Each wildcard becomes `%P1..`.
- **simple**: the line must equal the pattern exactly.
- **regexp**: Go (RE2) syntax, matches anywhere in the line, `%P0..`, `%PL`, `%PR`.

Dispatch: matching macros are ordered by priority (high first), then definition
order. The first one fires; if it has `-F` the next fires too, and so on. Only
one macro per priority level fires unless `-F` is used (a deliberate
simplification: TF picks randomly among equals). A hook fires its macros the
same way; hook arguments become `%1..`.

Other macro commands:

| Command                                                 |                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/undef name...`                                        | remove macros by name                                                     |
| `/undefn N...`                                          | remove by number shown in `/list`                                         |
| `/list [-s] [glob]`                                     | list definitions (`-s`: names only)                                       |
| `/purge [glob]`                                         | remove all (or matching) macros                                           |
| `/enable name...` `/disable name...`                    | extension: switch a macro off/on without deleting it                      |
| `/gag pattern` / `/hilite pattern`                      | define a `-g` / `-a$hiliteattr` trigger                                   |
| `/trigger [-w world] text`                              | run triggers as if `text` had arrived                                     |
| `/trigpc chance priority text`                          | like `/trigger` with a probability, only macros of at least that priority |
| `/bind key = command`, `/unbind key`, `/dokey name`     | key bindings; `/dokey` asks the host to perform a key action              |
| `/save file [glob]`, `/load [-q] file`, `/require file` | files (gated by `/restrict`)                                              |

Redefining a name replaces the macro and fires the `REDEF` hook. A macro name
shadows a built-in command of the same name; `/builtin name args` runs the
built-in.

topics.title: Attributes
topics.body:
An attribute string is a comma-separated list; each item is flag letters
optionally followed by one colour clause:

| Item                    | Meaning                                              |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `n`                     | normal: reset styling first                          |
| `h` or `B`              | bold                                                 |
| `d` `i` `u` `s` `f` `r` | dim, italic, underline, strike, flash/blink, reverse |
| `g`                     | gag                                                  |
| `C<colour>`             | foreground colour                                    |
| `BC<colour>`            | background colour                                    |

Colours: `black red green yellow blue magenta cyan white` (0-7), `bright` + name
(8-15), a palette index `0`..`255` (xterm-256), `rgbRGB` (6x6x6 cube, digits
0-5, e.g. `rgb530`), `gray0`..`gray23`, and 24-bit `#rrggbb` or `#rgb`.

```
/echo -aCred,u red underlined
/echo -aC196 palette 196
/echo -aC#ff8800,BC#001122 truecolour on truecolour
/def -t'*dragon*' -ahC#ff4040 dragon
/def -mregexp -t'(\d+) gold' -P1BCyellow,C0 gold
```

**Inline markup** (`/echo -p`, `echo()`, `encode_attr`): `@{attrs}` changes the
current attributes (they accumulate; `@{n}` resets), `@@` is a literal `@`:
`/echo -p @{Cred}red@{n} plain @{C#00ff00}green`.

topics.title: Control flow
topics.body:
```
/if (expr) commands
/elseif (expr) commands
/else commands
/endif

/while (expr)        ; /do directly after the header is optional
  ...
/done

/do
  ...
/while (expr)

/for var first last commands /done
/break      /return [expr]
```

Commands after a header on the same line are the first statements of that body;
separate statements with `%;` inside macro bodies:

```
/def count = /let i=1 %; /while (i <= {1}) %; /echo %i %; /let i=$[i+1] %; /done
```

(`/let` and `/set` store text: `/let i=i+1` would store the string `i+1`; use
`$[...]` to compute.)
A typed line closes unfinished blocks at its end; in a script file an
unfinished block is an error. Every run is limited (section 10).

topics.title: Commands
topics.body:
`/help` lists them and `/help name` prints usage.

- Output: `/echo [-w world] [-a attrs] [-p] text`, `/send [-w world] text`,
  `/beep`, `/notify title | body` (extension), `/gag`, `/hilite`.
- Variables/eval: `/set /setenv /export /unset /let /listvar /shift [n]
/eval /test /return /break /builtin`.
- Macros/files: see section 5.
- Timers: `/repeat [-w world] -<seconds|m:s|h:m:s> <count> <command>` runs a
  command repeatedly through the host's timer service (`/repeat 3 cmd` without a
  time runs it three times now); `/ps` lists timers, `/kill id` stops one.
- `/quote [-dsend|echo|exec] [prefix] 'file` runs each line of a file (needs file
  access) and `/quote [prefix] #command` each line a command echoes; every line
  becomes `prefix + line`. Shell forms (`!cmd`, `` `cmd` ``) are not available.
- Worlds (need world access): `/addworld [-Ttype] [-x] name [char pass] host port`,
  `/connect [world]`, `/dc [world]`, `/fg [world]`, `/world name`, `/unworld`,
  `/listworlds [glob]`, `/listsockets`, `/saveworld`.
- UI delegates (the host decides what they do): `/limit /unlimit /relimit
/recall /log /input /localecho /status_add /status_edit /status_rm /dokey
/histsize`.
- `/version /features /help /restrict [shell|file|world] /exit /quit`.

`/restrict` raises (never lowers) the restriction level: `shell` (always in
force; there is no shell access), `file` (no `/load /save /quote 'file /log`),
`world` (also no world/connection commands). The application sets the initial
level (`Options.Restrict`).

topics.title: Functions
topics.body:
Strings: `strlen strcat strcmp strncmp strchr strrchr strstr strrep substr pad
tolower toupper replace substitute ascii char` (indices are in characters, 0
based; `strchr(s, set)` is the first position of any character of `set`, or -1;
`pad(s, w)` right-justifies in `w` columns, a negative width left-justifies;
`replace(old, new, s)` replaces every occurrence of old in s (TF argument order); `substitute(text [, attrs [,
inline]])` replaces the line being processed by a trigger).

Regexp: `regmatch(pattern, string)` returns 1/0 and sets `%P0..%P9`, `%PL`, `%PR`
for the rest of the macro.

Math: `abs sin cos tan asin acos atan exp ln log10 pow sqrt rand trunc mod`
(`rand(n)` is 0..n-1; `rand(a, b)` is inclusive).

Time: `time()` (Unix seconds), `mktime(y,m,d,h,mi,s)`, `ftime(format [, secs])`
(strftime codes `%Y %y %m %d %e %H %I %M %S %p %a %A %b %B %j %Z %z %s %F %T %R
%D %c %n %t %%`), `idle([world])` seconds since last input, `sidle([world])`
since last send.

Misc: `eval(str)` (expand and run as commands, returns the echoed text), `test(expr)`,
`whatis(v)` (`int`, `float`, `str`), `getopts(optstring [, args])` (sets locals
`opt_x`, returns the remaining arguments), `echo(str [, attrs [, inline [, world]]])`,
`send(str [, world])`, `prompt(str)`, `world_info([world,] field)` (`name host port
character type tls connected`), `is_connected([world])`, `is_open`, `fg_world()`,
`nactive()`, `columns()`, `lines()`, `winlines()`, `isatty()`, `systype()`.

Attributes: `encode_attr(text, attrs)`, `decode_attr(text)` (markup to an ANSI
string with 16/256/24-bit codes), `strip_attr(text)` (remove markup and ANSI).

topics.title: Hooks
topics.body:
`/def -hNAME [argpattern] name = body`. Names: `ACTIVITY ATCP BAMF BGTEXT BGTRIG
CONFAIL CONFLICT CONNECT DISCONNECT GMCP ICONFAIL KILL LOAD LOADFAIL LOG LOGIN
MAIL MORE NOMACRO OPTION102 PENDING PREACTIVITY PROCESS PROMPT PROXY REDEF RESIZE
SEND SHADOW SHELL SIGHUP SIGTERM SIGUSR1 SIGUSR2 WORLD`. The application fires
them with `FireHook(name, args...)`; the engine fires `CONNECT DISCONNECT CONFAIL
LOGIN WORLD SEND PROMPT ACTIVITY BGTEXT BGTRIG LOAD REDEF RESIZE GMCP`. The
interpreter itself fires `SEND` (before text is sent; a SEND hook that sends does
not recurse), `LOAD`, `LOADFAIL` and `REDEF`. `/hook NAME args` fires a hook by
hand; `/hook` lists names. Hook arguments are `%1..`, e.g. `GMCP` gets
`%1` = package, `%2` = JSON.

topics.title: Limits and safety
topics.body:
Every top-level run (an input line, a received line, a hook, a key, a timer, one
logical line of a loaded file) has:

- a step budget (statements, loop iterations, expression evaluations, function
  calls; default 50 000),
- a wall deadline on the host clock (default 2 s),
- a macro nesting limit (default 64) and file nesting limit (16),
- a 256 KB cap on any one string value.

Exceeding a limit aborts that run with `% script budget exceeded: ...`; the
interpreter stays usable. When a received line is replayed from scrollback
(`live=false`) no macro body runs, nothing is sent or notified, no shot is
consumed and no variable is changed; only gag and highlight are computed.

topics.title: Examples
topics.body:
```
; keep-alive every five minutes
/def -hCONNECT on_connect = /repeat -300 100000 /send IDLE
; highlight tells and notify
/def -mregexp -t'^(\w+) tells you: (.*)$' -P1Cbrightgreen,h tell = \
    /notify Tell from %P1 | %P2
; gag spam, but only from one world
/def -wmain -t'\[Spam\]*' -g spam
; auto-loot with a condition and a 50% chance
/def -t'* is dead.' -E'looting' -c50 loot = get all from corpse
; 256 and truecolour
/def -t'*ALERT*' -a'BC#400000,C#ffe0e0,h' alert
; a helper with a return value
/def max = /return {1} > {2} ? {1} : {2}
/echo biggest: $[max(3, 9)]
```

topics.title: Host integration (Go)
topics.body:
See `pkg/tf/doc.go` and `host.go`: implement `tf.Host` (embed `tf.NopHost`),
`tf.New(host, tf.Options{...})`, then `Exec`, `OnLine(world, line, live)`,
`FireHook`, `Key`, `LoadFile`/`LoadString`, `Vars/GetVar/SetVar/ExportVars/
ImportVars`, `Macros`. All calls are serialised; host callbacks must not call
back into the interpreter.

topics.title: Reading the matrix
topics.body:
Status legend: **Done** (works as described in `TF-LANGUAGE.md`), **Partial**
(works with the stated difference), **Planned (P2)**, **GUI** (replaced by a GUI
feature, the host decides), **N/A** (not applicable to this client).

`pkg/tf` is a clean-room implementation inspired by TinyFugue's documented
behaviour; it contains no TinyFugue code or help text. The checklist is the
list in `squatClient/docs/DESIGN.md` section 3.2. Those lists were written from
TinyFugue's `cmdlist.h`, `funclist.h`, `hooklist.h`, `varlist.h`; the semantics
below were implemented from knowledge of the public manual, **not verified
against a reference binary yet** (the oracle differential tests of DESIGN 3.5
are not set up), so treat every "Done" as "implemented to the documented
intent". Where TF's exact behaviour was uncertain the most sensible semantics
were chosen and are noted here.

topics.title: Deliberate differences (read these first)
topics.body:
| Area                      | TinyFugue-style                                  | Here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Expression substitution   | `%` text substitution happens inside expressions | Inside `$[..]`, `/if (..)` etc. `%x`, `%1`, `%*`, `%{x}` are **variable references** (never re-parsed as expression text); `%` is not interpolated in string literals. Removes a code-injection hazard from MUD text.                                                                            |
| `=~` `!~` `=/` `!/`       | as defined by TF                                 | `=~`/`!~`: exact string equal / not equal. `=/`/`!/`: **glob** match (pattern on the right). Regexps via `regmatch()` or `-mregexp`.                                                                                                                                                             |
| No modulo operator        | n/a                                              | use `mod()`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Trigger firing            | one random macro among equal priorities          | deterministic: priority desc, then definition order; the first fires, `-F` continues. Only one macro per priority level fires unless `-F`.                                                                                                                                                       |
| Glob captures             | none                                             | every wildcard of a glob trigger is `%P1..` (`%P0` the whole line).                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Statement splitting       |                                                  | text lines (not starting `/`) are never split at `;`; `/def`, `/repeat`, `/eval` keep `%;` for later.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Script files              | non-command lines are sent as text               | non-command lines in a loaded file are an **error** (no accidental sends). Unclosed blocks in a file are an error.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Error handling            |                                                  | errors are reported as `% msg` and execution continues, but an error inside a loop body ends the loop; max 20 errors shown per run.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `/def` of a built-in name |                                                  | the macro shadows the built-in; `/builtin cmd` reaches the built-in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `%{N}` / `%{-N}` ranges   |                                                  | `%{-N}` and `%{N-}` style ranges are **not** implemented. `%0` is the macro name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `$(command)`              | command substitution                             | returns the echoed lines joined by spaces, else the `/return` value. Backquote `` `cmd` `` substitution is **not** implemented (it implied a shell).                                                                                                                                             |
| Time zones                | system TZ                                        | `TZ` supports `UTC` and fixed offsets only (the package does no I/O, so no zoneinfo).                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `pad()`                   |                                                  | positive width right-justifies, negative left-justifies, no truncation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

topics.title: Policy: terminal-only TinyFugue features are out of scope
topics.body:
SquatClient is a GUI client. Anything TinyFugue has _only because it ran in a text terminal_ is **not implemented and not planned**.
Scripts that use them still load: the commands/variables are **accepted and ignored** (no error), so a `.tf` file written for the
terminal does not break here. Where a GUI equivalent exists, it is a UI setting, not a TF command.

| TF feature                                                                                                                                      | Why it is out                                  | Here                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `wrap`, `wraplog`, `wrapspace`, `wrapsize`                                                                                                      | Line wrapping is done by the window            | UI soft-wrap setting (settings.wrap); `wraplog` only affects `/log` text files             |
| `more`, `/more`-style paging, `morepaused`/`morescroll`/`moresize`                                                                              | Terminal paging prompt                         | UI "pause when scrolled up" (settings.pauseOnScroll); functions return 0/neutral values    |
| `/visual`, `visual`                                                                                                                             | Screen mode toggle; the GUI is always "visual" | no-op                                                                                      |
| `/redraw`, `/refresh`-style screen repaint, `/suspend`, `/core`, terminal signals (`SIGHUP`, `SIGTERM`, `SIGUSR*` hooks)                        | Terminal/process control                       | no-op / N/A                                                                                |
| Terminal geometry: status line rows, `status_width` layout details, `isatty`, `termcap`/`TERM` handling, `/lcd`-style cursor handling           | Terminal-specific                              | status _fields_ are kept (they drive the GUI status bar); geometry is the window's concern |
| Keyboard-buffer functions (`kbhead kbtail kbpoint kbgoto kbdel kblen kbmatch kbwordleft kbwordright kb_visual_move`) and `kb*.tf`-style keymaps | Input line is a GUI widget                     | low priority: may be exposed later over the input widget; not required                     |
| `/sh`, `/quote !`, `/ps`/`/kill` process commands                                                                                               | Shell access                                   | kept only behind `/restrict` (default: denied), not terminal-dependent                     |

`columns()` and `lines()` are kept and return the output pane's size in characters (useful to scripts); NAWS uses the same numbers.

topics.title: Overview of the API
topics.body:
SquatClient embeds Lua 5.1 (gopher-lua, pure Go) as a sandboxed scripting language alongside the TF engine.
Scripts are plain `.lua` files so they can later be synced to a daemon (see `AUTOMATION.md`).

topics.title: Basics
topics.body:
- Everything lives in the global table `squat`. Each plugin gets its **own** global environment: globals you
  assign are private to your plugin, and changing `string`, `table` or `math` never affects other plugins.
- All scripts run on one thread, one at a time. You never need locks.
- Every call into your code (a trigger, a handler, a timer tick, loading the file) has a **budget**
  (about 5 million VM instructions and 500 ms wall-clock by default). Exceeding it aborts that call with an
  error in the log; the client keeps running and your other handlers still work.
- Errors in one plugin never stop another plugin.

## The `live` rule (important)

A line can be **live** (just arrived) or **replayed** (scrollback/backlog re-processed after reattaching).
Replayed lines only get _display effects_: `gag`, highlight colours, and spans returned by `line` handlers.
On replayed lines:

- trigger `fn` callbacks are **not called**;
- `line`/`prompt` handlers _are_ called (with `l.live == false`) so they can restyle or gag, but
  `squat.send`, `echo`, `notify`, `tf`, `var.set`, `var.del`, `after`, `timer`, `on`, `trigger`, `alias` and
  `remove` do nothing and return `false`.

Write line handlers so they compute the display result from the text, and put side effects in trigger `fn`s.

topics.title: Sandbox
topics.body:
Available: base functions (`pairs`, `pcall`, `error`, `setmetatable`, `tostring`, `unpack` ...), `string`,
`table`, `math`, `coroutine`, and a restricted `os` with only `time`, `date`, `clock`, `difftime`
(driven by the client clock). `print(...)` goes to the log.

Not available: `io`, `debug`, `package`, `os.execute/remove/rename/getenv/exit`, `dofile`, `loadfile`,
`string.dump`, `getfenv/setfenv`, `module`, `newproxy`, native modules. `loadstring`/`load` work but compile into your
own environment and refuse binary chunks. `string.rep` results are capped (4 MiB).

`require("name")` loads `name.lua` (dots become `/`) from **your plugin's own directory** only.

topics.title: Output and sending
topics.body:
| Call                           | Meaning                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `squat.send(text [, world])`   | Send a line to the game. Returns `true`, or `nil, err`.                                 |
| `squat.echo(x [, world])`      | Show text locally. `x` is a string, one span `{s="..."}`, or an array of spans/strings. |
| `squat.notify(title [, body])` | Desktop notification.                                                                   |
| `squat.log(text [, level])`    | Write to the client log; level is `"info"`, `"warn"` or `"error"`.                      |
| `squat.world()`                | Display name of the world the current line/event belongs to.                            |
| `squat.now()`                  | Seconds since the Unix epoch (float) from the client clock.                             |

`world` defaults to the world of the line/event being handled (timers remember the world they were created in).
Calling `send`/`echo`/`tf` with no current world and no `world` argument is an error.

## Spans and colours

A span is a table: `{s="text", fg=..., bg=..., b=true, dim=, i=, u=, st=, blink=, rev=, link="url"}`.

- `fg`/`bg` is an integer **0-255** (xterm-256 palette index; 0-15 follow the theme) or a string
  **`"#rrggbb"`** for 24-bit truecolor. Both survive the round trip to the display exactly; no quantisation.
- Anything else (`256`, `1.5`, `"red"`, `"#abc"`) is an error.

topics.title: Events: squat.on(event, fn [, priority])
topics.body:
| Event                   | `fn` receives                                              |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `line`                  | `{text, spans, world, prompt, live}`                       |
| `prompt`                | the same, only for flushed prompts                         |
| `connect`, `disconnect` | `{world, ...}` (fields chosen by the engine)               |
| `gmcp`                  | `{package, data, raw, world}` (`data` is the decoded JSON) |
| `input`                 | `{text, world}`; return `true` to swallow the input        |
| `timer`                 | engine tick payload                                        |

Line handlers may modify the line:

```lua
squat.on("line", function(l)
  if l.text:find("spam") then return {gag = true} end
  l.spans = {{s = "[!] ", fg = 196}, unpack(l.spans)}   -- assign a new table (in-place edits are not seen)
end)
```

Return `{gag=true}` to hide the line, `{spans=...}` to replace it, `{stop=true}` to stop later rules.
A gag does **not** stop later rules (so a gagged line can still trigger an auto-heal).

**Ordering:** triggers and `line` handlers form one list, run by `priority` (higher first, default 0), then in
registration order. This is deterministic and identical on live and replayed lines.

`squat.on` returns an id; `squat.remove(id)` (alias `squat.cancel`) unregisters it.

topics.title: Triggers and aliases
topics.body:
```lua
squat.trigger{
  match    = "You are hit by * for * damage.",  -- glob unless regex=true
  regex    = false,        -- true: RE2 regular expression (unanchored search)
  icase    = false,        -- case-insensitive
  gag      = false,        -- hide the line (display effect, also on replay)
  fg = "#ff8800", bg = 17, b = true, u = true,   -- highlight (display effect, also on replay)
  hilite   = "line",       -- "line" (default) or "match": colour only the matched text
  world    = "MyMUSH",     -- optional: only this world (name or id)
  priority = 0,
  fn       = function(m) ... end,   -- optional, live lines only
}
```

**Glob:** matches the whole line; `*` matches any run (captured), `?` one character, `\*` and `\?` are literal.
**Regex:** Go RE2 syntax (<https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax>): linear-time, no backreferences or
lookaround; named groups `(?P<name>...)`.

`fn(m)` gets `m.text`, `m[0]` (whole match), `m[1..n]` (captures; `""` if a group did not take part),
`m.named.<name>`, `m.world`, `m.live`, `m.spans`, `m.prompt`. It may return `{gag=true}`/`{spans=...}`/`{stop=true}`.

Aliases run on text the user typed:

```lua
squat.alias{match = "k *", fn = function(m) squat.send("kill " .. m[1]) end}
```

Same match options (`regex`, `icase`, `world`, `priority`). An alias handles the input (it is not sent) unless
its function returns `false`; the first handling alias wins.

topics.title: Timers
topics.body:
```lua
squat.timer{every = 30, count = 5, fn = function() ... end}   -- count omitted: repeat forever
squat.after(2.5, function() ... end)                          -- once
local id = squat.timer{...};  squat.cancel(id)
```

Intervals are seconds (minimum 0.05 by default, at most 512 live timers). Timers are scheduled through the
client host and use its clock; they are removed on plugin reload. A tick that errors is logged and the timer keeps going.

topics.title: Variables
topics.body:
`squat.var.get(name [, default])`, `squat.var.set(name, value)`, `squat.var.del(name)`, `squat.var.keys()`.
Values are strings, numbers, booleans, or tables of those (JSON-compatible; functions and cycles are rejected).
`set(name, nil)` deletes. The store belongs to the engine, is shared by all plugins (prefix your names), survives
`/reload`, and is exported/imported as JSON (`Runtime.ExportVars/ImportVars`).

topics.title: Regular expressions
topics.body:
`squat.regex.match(pattern, text)` returns `nil` or a table `m[0]`, `m[1..n]`, `m.named`;
`squat.regex.test(pattern, text)` returns a boolean; `squat.regex.replace(pattern, text, repl)` uses `$1`/`${name}`.

topics.title: Talking to TF
topics.body:
`squat.tf(code [, world])` runs one line of TinyFugue input in the TF engine (`true` or `nil, err`).
TF's `/lua <code>` runs Lua in a persistent console environment (engine wiring: `Runtime.Exec`, or
`Runtime.ExecInCallback` when TF was itself called from Lua).

topics.title: Plugins
topics.body:
```
plugins/
  heal.lua              a single-file plugin named "heal"
  combat/
    plugin.json         {"name": "combat", "version": "1.0", "description": "...", "enabled": true, "main": "main.lua"}
    main.lua            entry point (default main.lua, then init.lua)
    util.lua            require("util")
```

`plugin.json` is optional; `"enabled": false` skips the plugin. A plugin that fails to load is reported and skipped.
`/reload` discards all handlers, timers and plugin globals and re-runs every plugin from disk.

topics.title: Examples
topics.body:
The scripts below are in `testdata/lua/` and are exercised by the test suite.

Auto-heal:

```lua
squat.trigger{
  match = "^HP: (\\d+)/(\\d+)", regex = true,
  fn = function(m)
    local hp, max = tonumber(m[1]), tonumber(m[2])
    if hp / max < 0.4 and squat.now() - squat.var.get("last_heal", 0) > 3 then
      squat.var.set("last_heal", squat.now())
      squat.send("cast heal")
    end
  end,
}
```

Truecolor highlight:

```lua
squat.trigger{match = "*tells you*", fg = "#ff8800", b = true}
squat.trigger{match = "treasure", regex = true, hilite = "match", fg = "#ffd700", bg = 52}
```

Gag spam (still counting it on live lines):

```lua
squat.trigger{match = "^<Spam> ", regex = true, gag = true,
  fn = function() squat.var.set("spam_count", squat.var.get("spam_count", 0) + 1) end}
```

Timer (anti-idle, per connection):

```lua
squat.on("connect", function() squat.timer{every = 300, fn = function() squat.send("") end} end)
```

Alias:

```lua
squat.alias{match = "k *", fn = function(m) squat.send("kill " .. m[1]) end}
```

Call TF:

```lua
squat.trigger{match = "* arrives.", fn = function(m) squat.tf("/echo -aB Welcome, " .. m[1] .. "!") end}
```

topics.title: Limits (what the budget can and cannot stop)
topics.body:
Enforced per call: VM instruction count (main thread), wall-clock timeout (also stops coroutines), heap-growth
ceiling (sampled every 65536 instructions, process-wide so approximate), Lua call depth and stack size,
`string.rep` size, timer/variable counts. **Not** interruptible: a single long-running built-in such as a
pathological `string.find` pattern or very wide `string.format`; the call is marked failed when it returns, but it
can still occupy the (single) script thread until then. Prefer `squat.regex` (RE2, linear time) for untrusted patterns.
